summary.headline: MPS raised FY27 EBITDA floor to at least INR 310 crore; H1 revenue up 17.8% to INR 448.5 crore at a 34.3% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 was described as the most profitable half in MPS history, with revenue up 17.8% to INR 448.5 crore and EBITDA up 39% to INR 154 crore at a 34.3% margin. Q2 revenue was roughly flat sequentially, which management attributed to timing: large research mandates only begin billing in November and December, and Education and Corporate Learning follow adoption calendars. Management raised its FY27 EBITDA floor from above INR 300 crore to at least INR 310 crore, and reiterated the INR 1,500 crore FY28 revenue ambition, which now depends on an acquisition expected to close this financial year. The company carries zero debt and INR 163 crore of cash.

segments.name: Research Solutions
segments.commentary: Margin 48.2% in Q2, up more than 6 points YoY. Excluding AJE, revenue grew about 22% at a margin close to 50%, with no acquisitions in that figure. A large new production mandate and a research integrity mandate bill from November.

segments.name: Education Solutions
segments.commentary: Now 30.6% of group revenue; H1 revenue +36%, EBITDA +14.5%. Bookings led by Florida's upcoming math adoption, with California to follow. Unbound contributed INR 41.6 crore in H1 and its margin rose from 12-13% at acquisition to about 18%.

segments.name: Corporate Learning
segments.commentary: H1 margin rose to 25% from about 16%, with EBITDA up 77% and 19% fewer people. Q2 revenue grew 17%. A four-year program with a large US university was won, combining Unbound and Liberate.

segments.name: AJE (within Research)
segments.commentary: Acquired for about INR 70 crore in February 2024; management estimates payback at 2 to 2.5 years, with EBITDA margin upwards of 30% and more than half of the purchase price earned annually. Pre-submission peer review launched in April 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA floor raised to at least INR 310 crore from above INR 300 crore; management cites H1 doubled at about INR 308 crore and historically stronger H2, with Q4 above Q3.
Guidance assumes an exchange rate well below current levels, so the floor does not depend on currency.

FY28 revenue target of INR 1,500 crore reiterated; management says it combines organic growth and acquisitions, and expects the next acquisition to close in FY27 and will give a tighter FY28 view then.
Capital allocation: growth, including acquisitions, is the first priority this year; distributions resume once capital is deployed; capital must earn its return within 12 months.
Management targets a 'Rule of 50' (growth plus EBITDA margin), above 50 in H1, and measures the full year against that bar.
capex_capacity: Hiring ahead of the new research mandates to ensure reliable delivery; headcount rising, while EBITDA per employee rose about 15% in Q2.
Sales FTEs and marketing budgets are being expanded; product development and tech stack spend is fully expensed, with nothing capitalised.
Pre-submission peer review launched at AJE in April 2026; more author solutions built around research integrity planned before end of FY27.
ISO 42001 AI governance certification obtained in September 2026; more than 200 engineers build AI in-house.
Unbound's next move is into hospitals and health systems; a mobile companion app for first-year nurses is in development.
demand_pricing: Research demand is strongest in research integrity and peer review; a large customer is moving more than 110,000 submissions a year onto MPS's peer review platform.

Contract lives in research are typically three to five years. Pricing is shared with customers on productivity, offset by volume; management says throughput, not pricing, is the main customer consideration.
Education demand follows the US state adoption calendar; bookings are order intake, not yet revenue.
Corporate Learning budgets are rising around AI; focus areas are healthcare workforce learning and APAC, where new logos were added in H1.
Management says more than one in five new US hospital nurses leaves within the first year, at a replacement cost of about USD 60,000.

qa_highlights.question: With no acquisition announced since Unbound, how is progress toward the INR 1,500 crore FY28 target, and where is the next deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target combines organic growth and acquisitions and expects the next acquisition to close this financial year. It has walked away from deals priced above what it considers their worth, and has zero debt and INR 163 crore cash.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Unbound niche criteria for future acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Assets must have AI tailwinds, operate in science or high-stakes content, have low customer concentration, a recurring revenue theme, a defensible niche, and a clear way to plug into MPS.

qa_highlights.question: Why was sequential revenue almost flat in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to timing: new research mandates bill from November and December, and Education and Corporate Learning follow adoption and project timing. Growth is expected to build in H2, with Q4 weighted.

qa_highlights.question: How could a Democratic Congress affect MPS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to make deep NIH and NSF cuts less likely and to protect federal nursing workforce programs, which the administration had proposed cutting about 70%. It sees this as a positive for research, healthcare, and education demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI causing pricing pressure in research, and are clients reluctant to sign longer contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts remain three to five years and pricing is a win-win in which lower rates are offset by volume. Throughput, not price, is the main client consideration.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Unbound margin lever progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbound margin rose from 12-13% at acquisition to about 18%. The next step toward the 20s is expected to come from revenue growth rather than cost cuts.

qa_highlights.question: Why is AJE still struggling to grow, and what is its payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AJE is strategically important as the AI language engine and an entry point to research integrity work. Payback on the roughly INR 70 crore purchase is estimated at 2 to 2.5 years, and ROCE is about 35%.

risks_watch: INR 1,500 crore FY28 revenue target requires an acquisition still not announced; a tighter view is promised after the next deal closes.
Q2 revenue was flat sequentially; H2 growth depends on new research mandates billing from November and on the timing of the US adoption calendar.
AJE growth remains weak despite rightsizing, although management describes it as financially successful.
Margin depends on volume offsetting AI-driven price pressure while SG&A, sales headcount and marketing spend rise.
Q3 FY27 results are the next checkpoint for the new INR 310 crore EBITDA floor and the Unbound margin trajectory.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and the EBITDA floor, but more cautious on near-term revenue, which management attributes to timing. Management was defensive on acquisition pace and on AJE growth, pointing to payback and strategic value rather than current growth.
key_quotes: For six quarters, our earnings have grown much faster than our revenue, and the reason is what MPS has become: an AI-first knowledge company that owns its platforms and its IP, and is paid for outcomes.
We would rather miss a deal than overpay.
AI hollows out businesses that sell hours. We sell outcomes.
The first half of FY'27 was the most profitable half-year in the history of MPS.
